pointers.sentence: It is a method of the handler, `BaseHandler._get_response`: in its docstring's words, everything that happens inside the request and response middleware (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

`BaseHandler.resolve_request` picks a resolver, asks it to match the request's `path_info`, which is the path without the script prefix, and stores the answer on the request (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`).
When nothing matches, the resolver raises `Resolver404`, which is a subclass of `Http404` (`django/urls/exceptions.py:Resolver404`).
`CsrfViewMiddleware` does its checking here for that reason: whether a view is exempt is an attribute of the view (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`).
An async view cannot be wrapped this way: the method raises `RuntimeError` if it finds one while a database asks for atomic requests (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.make_view_atomic`).

If it raises an `Exception`, the handler passes the exception to `BaseHandler.process_exception_by_middleware`, which calls the `process_exception` hooks, innermost middleware first, until one returns a response (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.process_exception_by_middleware`).
Each raises a `ValueError` whose message names the view (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.check_response`).
